subject: Acme Payments latency review and credit evaluation
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@acmepay.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2028 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Intermittent high tail latency impacting Checkout (possible SLA claim)

Jonas —

We saw a pronounced tail-latency spike on Checkout today that correlated with a brief but material customer impact. Our monitoring shows a surge of requests hitting >2s at 09:14:00 UTC and sustained elevated latencies through roughly 09:31:00 UTC, with a small increase in 5xxs reported by our auth/payment gateway (approx 0.7% of requests). That window maps to several failed and delayed checkouts; our estimate based on transaction volumes is ~50k USD/hr impact during the window.

I’m attaching a CSV of sample request_ids and a performance trace bundle. Can you confirm whether this meets Redwood’s availability/latency SLA criteria and what the next steps are for credit evaluation and a post-incident report? We need a timeline for the postmortem for our execs.

Attachments: acmepay_request_ids_20280115.csv, perf_trace_20280115.tar.gz

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Patel
Head of Platform Ops, Acme Payments
support@acmepay.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@acmepay.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2028 09:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Intermittent high tail latency impacting Checkout (possible SLA claim)

Sara — thanks for the heads up and for sending the IDs. We’re pulling the traces and will validate the request set against our edge and origin logs.

Quick answers up front:
- We’ll verify the exact impact window and whether the observed behavior triggers the latency availability clause in your contract.
- Assuming verification, we’ll open a credit evaluation and produce a postmortem with root cause and mitigations.

Can you confirm the timezone you used for the timestamps in the CSV (I assume UTC) and whether you have any customer-facing incidents (support tickets) tied to the same request IDs? Karthik, can you take point on pulling the cluster metrics and qcache traces for 09:00–10:00 UTC? Evelyn, please log this as an SLA review and add it to the incident backlog (JIRA-INC-8241).

We’ll aim to provide an initial eligibility determination within 3 business days and a fuller postmortem within 10 business days unless the investigation scope changes.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@acmepay.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2028 10:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Intermittent high tail latency impacting Checkout (possible SLA claim)

Jonas — thanks, UTC is correct for the CSV timestamps. I’ve also included links to two Zendesk tickets (ZD-11234, ZD-11237) raised by merchants during the window. Those tickets reference the request_ids in the CSV.

For context: we saw a sharp latency tail starting at 09:14:07 UTC and traffic returned to baseline ~09:31:20 UTC. Error percentages remain low overall but a small subset of checkout flows experienced timeouts and retries. We need confirmation whether this constitutes a latency SLO breach and, if so, how any credit would be calculated so we can start our internal accounting.

Attachments: acmepay_request_ids_20280115.csv, perf_trace_20280115.tar.gz

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

—Sara
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@acmepay.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jan 2028 11:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Intermittent high tail latency impacting Checkout (possible SLA claim)

Sara — we completed an initial verification against our telemetry and your supplied request IDs. Summary below; full evidence bundle attached.

Summary of findings (preliminary):
- Verified elevated P99/P999 latencies that map to your request_ids. The anomalous window in our logs is 2028-01-15T09:14:07Z through 2028-01-15T09:31:22Z.
- Root cause (initial): transient KV-cache compaction coupled with a short-lived routing imbalance on one serving shard; this amplified tail latency for a subset of in-flight requests.
- Impact: according to the SLA metric (requests over 2s), the affected window exceeds the permitted threshold for your committed tier, so this is a potential eligibility for remediation/credit under the contract. Final credit calculation requires aggregation across your full account usage for the billing period.

Next steps and timing:
1) We’re opening a formal SLA claim ticket and will calculate the preliminary credit amount; expect an update on the dollar-equivalent credit in 5 business days.
2) We’ll produce a customer-facing postmortem doc with timeline, RCA, and mitigations within 10 business days. Draft will be shared with you for review before publication.
3) Immediate mitigation: we’ve pushed a patch to reduce compaction-trigger sensitivity and adjusted routing thresholds to avoid the shard imbalance recurrence.

Attachments: redwood_prelim_evidence_bundle.zip (contains server-side traces, compaction logs, and request id crosswalk)

If you have specific format requirements for the postmortem or a preferred contact for the credit discussion (finance/P.O. routing), send them over and we’ll include that in the claim ticket.

Thanks for flagging this and for the evidence you provided — it materially sped the verification.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
